components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The primary action; runway cyan on obsidian text. Used sparingly — one per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Inter Display', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; background: var(--primary, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.18 0.03 254)); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25); transition: background 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--ring, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action on the obsidian floor; fills amber on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Inter Display', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; background: var(--background, oklch(0.19 0.03 254)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.97 0.01 240)); border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.28 0.03 254)); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25); transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent, oklch(0.78 0.16 70)); color: var(--accent-foreground, oklch(0.18 0.03 254)); border-color: transparent; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--ring, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)); }

components.name: Card
components.description: Raised container one tonal step above the floor.
components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.32 0.03 254)); background: var(--card, oklch(0.22 0.03 254)); color: var(--card-foreground, oklch(0.97 0.01 240)); padding: 24px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25); font-family: 'Inter Display', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; line-height: 1; } .ds-card-desc { margin-top: 6px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.72 0.03 240)); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Transparent field with hull-border stroke; cyan focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { display: flex; width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(0.28 0.03 254)); background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.97 0.01 240)); font-family: 'Inter Display', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25); transition: box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.72 0.03 240)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--ring, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Small emphatic label; mono status variant uses tinted fill inside a tinted border.
components.css: .ds-badge-mono { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 4px; padding: 1px 6px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 9px; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: var(--primary, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)) 15%, transparent); border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.82 0.15 200)) 40%, transparent); }

narrative.overview: Flow Designer is a control tower rendered as software. The whole surface sits in a deep, cool obsidian where the only things that glow carry information. A single runway cyan reads as the live, primary signal; a warm warning amber reads as attention. This is an Operate surface first — operators and customers come to complete a task, and the design makes state instantly legible and never competes with it. The system is calm at rest and expressive only under state: depth comes from tonal layering rather than loud borders or shadow, and technical detail is set in JetBrains Mono for an honest instrument-panel texture. Because Atlas is the only source of truth, the language stays faithful and unembellished, and colour is never the sole carrier of meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Dark cockpit throughout; light is information, not decoration.
One rationed cyan primary + one amber attention accent; green/red/violet reserved for status.
Tonal layering over shadow for depth; soft glow only on live state.
Monospace for the machine, Inter Display for the human.
State is never colour alone — always hue + icon + label.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Runway cyan appears on ≤ ~10% of any screen. It is the primary/live colour and nothing else may borrow it; its rarity is what makes a single cyan ring legible on a crowded canvas.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: No state is communicated by hue alone. Running, waiting, succeeded, failed each pair their colour with an icon and an accessible label — the red ring is never the only issue signal.

rules.name: The Machine-Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything that is literally a value from Atlas — an ID, sequence cursor, byte count, edge condition, state token — is set in JetBrains Mono. Prose about the system stays in Inter Display.

rules.name: The Layered-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Reach for a lighter surface token before a bigger shadow. Shadows stay soft and ambient; glow is reserved for live state, never for ornament.

dos: Do reference semantic tokens, never literals — bg-card, text-primary, border-border. The one sanctioned exception is the canvas edge-label chip, which the renderer needs as fixed hex.
Do pair every state colour with an icon and an accessible label (aria-live for streaming status), and target WCAG 2.1 AA contrast.
Do set real Atlas values (IDs, cursors, counts, conditions) in JetBrains Mono; keep prose in Inter Display.
Do build depth by stepping surface tokens (obsidian -> raised -> slate) before adding shadow.
Do keep runway cyan rare — it means primary/live.
donts: Don't introduce a new hue for a status; the five signals (cyan/amber/green/red/violet) plus neutrals are the whole vocabulary.
Don't use colour as the only signal for a state, error, or node kind.
Don't hardcode bg-[#...], bg-black, or text-white; the global border reset and token layer already carry the theme.
Don't render an unbounded live/log list into one DOM tree — bound and incrementally render.
Don't spend cyan on decoration, or reach for a heavier shadow where a lighter surface token conveys the same lift.
